data.name: Security.av.none.Explanation
data.value: Turn on Microsoft Defender in Windows Security (Virus & threat protection), or install an antivirus.

data.name: Security.defender.realtime.Explanation
data.value: Turn it back on in Windows Security > Virus & threat protection > Manage settings. PCDoc does not change it itself, so that malware cannot use PCDoc to turn it off.

data.name: Security.defender.signatures.Explanation
data.value: Downloads the latest definitions from Microsoft.

data.name: Security.firewall.Explanation
data.value: Turns the Windows firewall back on. It blocks unwanted incoming connections.

data.name: Security.smb1.Explanation
data.value: Old file-sharing protocol used by ransomware such as WannaCry. Keep it only for a very old NAS or printer. Takes effect after a restart.

data.name: Security.ifeo.Explanation
data.value: A "Debugger" value makes Windows start another program instead of this one: a trick used by malware, but also by some tools (Process Explorer replacing the Task Manager).

data.name: Security.userinit.Title
data.value: The session start-up program was changed

data.name: Security.userinit.Explanation
data.value: Winlogon "Userinit" starts an extra program at each sign-in, a common malware trick (some company software does it too). Restores the Windows value.

data.name: Security.hosts.Title
data.value: The hosts file changes important websites

data.name: Security.hosts.Redirected
data.value: Microsoft or antivirus websites are sent to another address: often the work of malware. Check the lines below.

data.name: Security.hosts.Blocked
data.value: Microsoft or antivirus websites are blocked (often by an anti-tracking tool). Windows Update or your antivirus may not work properly.

data.name: Security.usb.Explanation
data.value: Shortcuts that start a script replace your folders, which were hidden. The shortcuts are disabled and your folders shown again (reversible). Then scan the drive with Defender.

data.name: Security.uac-on.Explanation
data.value: Without UAC every program runs with full rights. Turns it back on; takes effect after a restart.

data.name: Security.uac-prompt.Title
data.value: Programs can get administrator rights without asking

data.name: Security.uac-prompt.Explanation
data.value: Restores the Windows default: a confirmation is asked before a program gets full rights.

data.name: Security.autorun-off.Title
data.value: USB drives and CDs can start programs by themselves

data.name: Security.autorun-off.Explanation
data.value: Turns off AutoRun for all drives, the main way USB viruses spread. You can still open the drive yourself.

data.name: Security.smartscreen-on.Explanation
data.value: SmartScreen warns before running unknown downloaded programs. Turns the warning back on.

data.name: Security.rdp-off.Explanation
data.value: Other computers can connect to this PC. Turn it off if you do not use it.

data.name: Security.appinit-off.Title
data.value: DLLs are injected into every program (AppInit)

data.name: Security.appinit-off.Explanation
data.value: AppInit_DLLs loads a file into every program: used by malware and some old software. Turns loading off.

data.name: Security.winlogon-shell.Explanation
data.value: Winlogon "Shell" should be explorer.exe. Another value often starts malware at each sign-in. Restores explorer.exe.

data.name: Security.wdigest-off.Title
data.value: Passwords are kept in memory in clear text (WDigest)

data.name: Security.wdigest-off.Explanation
data.value: Lets password-stealing tools read your password. Turns it off (Windows default).

data.name: Security.Intro
data.value: Antivirus, firewall, places where malware hides, and USB drives.

data.name: Security.Scanning
data.value: Scanning… you can keep using the PC.

data.name: Security.ScanThreats
data.value: Scan finished: threats were found and handled by Defender. See the list below.

data.name: Security.ScanFailed
data.value: The scan could not run (Defender is off or replaced by another antivirus).
